decisions.reason: A low-cost web service built on the firm's existing address and grid databases costs little to carry, and with no adverse evidence its option value outweighs the upkeep.
The Austrian gas grid fee database extends the firm's core data offer into a new market whose uptake is still uncertain, so keeping this cheap option open is sensible.
Peak load window determination is a regulated, recurring calculation need of network operators that fits the firm's core competence and costs little to maintain.
An end-customer tariff database is close to the firm's market-data core and supports the platform strategy, and nothing in the evidence suggests its value has failed to materialize.
Custom web services are a flexible offering with low fixed carrying costs that feeds the move toward SaaS and integration.
A postal code lookup reuses existing data at minimal cost, though it is a commodity-like service that could be merged into broader platform modules.
